expectations.text: H1 same ingredients merged/summed when same unit, different units separate
expectations.evidence: S4: "the quantities are summed, e.g. 200 g flour + 300 g flour gives 500 g flour. With a different unit they stay separate entries ... Units are not converted".
S2: "using the **servings currently set** on the recipe, so quantities are scaled"; example: "A recipe for 4 servings, set to 2 servings, with 400 g Mehl: adding it puts 200 g Mehl on the list."

expectations.text: H3 one shared household list, check-offs visible to others within seconds
expectations.evidence: S1: "One shared list per household ... Changes by one member appear on the other members' devices within seconds, without a manual refresh."

expectations.text: H4 checked items move to bottom; 'finish shopping' clears checked items
expectations.evidence: S8: "Ticked entries move to the bottom of the list"; S10: "\"Liste leeren\". It removes **only the ticked entries**. Unticked entries stay."

expectations.text: H5 manual items can be added
expectations.evidence: S6: "A member can add free items that aren't in a recipe (e.g. \"Klopapier\"). Quantity and unit are optional."

expectations.text: H6 grouping by fixed supermarket sections
expectations.evidence: S11: "Unticked entries are grouped by section in this fixed walking order: Obst & Gemüse, Brot & Backwaren, ... Sonstiges." Caveat: demoted to "Should (desired, not a blocker; may ship in a later increment)" after the groomer's leading recommendation "Priorität: ... (Vorschlag: gewünscht, aber kein Blocker)"; stakeholder only said "wär schon nice" and then "Kein Blocker". Not contrary to brief (brief is silent on priority), so passed, but the with_skill run shows the true intent is a firm want.

expectations.text: Trap: 'Vorräte abhaken' captured as unticking at-home items when adding, not pantry/stock management
expectations.evidence: S3: "can deselect any they already have ... There is no pantry or stock tracking."; Non-goals: "No pantry or stock management". Stakeholder: "Nee, kein Vorratsmanagement, nur beim Hinzufügen wegklicken. Also a."

expectations.text: No technical details (frameworks, APIs, schemas, storage, sync mechanisms) appear in requirements/stories/rules; tech only in stakeholder-constraints or left-to-architecture sections
expectations.evidence: Stories are product-level (S9: "Changes sync automatically once the device is back online"). Firebase and sync approach appear only in "Constraints and notes for the architect".

expectations.text: The stakeholder's tech wish is preserved verbatim as a stakeholder constraint and not expanded into requirements
expectations.evidence: Not verbatim: "The stakeholder suggested **Firebase** for this, but only as an idea, not a hard requirement." No quote of "Sync am besten über Firebase". PERSONA DRIFT also involved: groomer asked a technical question ("Läuft die Rezept-App schon auf Firebase ... Ist Firebase ein Muss?") which the persona should have deflected; it answered "Firebase ist nur meine Idee dafür", and the doc then weakened the wish into "Choose the sync approach that fits the existing architecture best". Not expanded into requirements, though.

expectations.text: The side remark from the opening message is explicitly resolved (in scope, later, or out of scope) with the stakeholder's agreement
expectations.evidence: Q5 offered a/b/c/d; stakeholder: "Nee, kein Vorratsmanagement, nur beim Hinzufügen wegklicken. Also a." Reflected in S3 and Non-goals.

expectations.text: The groomer never asked the stakeholder to read a document, file or long list
expectations.evidence: No request to read a file/document. Post-write message asks to check 5 assumptions ("Bitte kurz prüfen") - short, not a document.

expectations.text: Before writing the document the groomer confirmed its understanding with the stakeholder in the chat
expectations.evidence: No confirmation before writing. The summary came after the file was written: "Danke, ist alles aufgeschrieben. Kurz zusammengefasst: ..." and "Falls etwas davon nicht passt, sag Bescheid."

expectations.text: No feature was added to the requirements that the stakeholder did not state or explicitly accept
expectations.evidence: "Later: \"Always at home\" list that is automatically skipped when adding recipes." - groomer suggested "b vielleicht später", stakeholder only answered "Also a." and never accepted b for later. Also unconfirmed-before-writing Assumptions, incl. one never mentioned in chat: "\"Same ingredient\" means the same name, ignoring upper/lower case", and quality rule "Ticking off must be fast with one hand" never discussed.

expectations.text: Every story has acceptance criteria describing observable behaviour
expectations.evidence: S1-S12 are one-line scope statements without their own ACs. Only 6 "Acceptance examples" exist; none for S6 manual entries, S7 edit/delete, S8 tick-off moving to bottom/untick, S11 section grouping order.

expectations.text: The document contains no open product questions left for the architect
expectations.evidence: S9: "So do adding, editing and deleting, as far as feasible" leaves the offline scope undecided; "Assumptions (confirm or correct during design if they cause trouble)" hands product decisions (merge identity, conflict rule, same recipe twice) to design; "Should ... may ship in a later increment" leaves the release scope of S11/S12 open.

expectations.text: Requirements document is written in English under docs/requirements/
